postings.listing_context: Research Fellow in Geo-Foundation Models Grade 7 £41,885 to £49,798 per annum 20/12/2026
postings.advert_text:
Research Fellow in Geo-Foundation Models

Are you excited by the potential of foundation models to transform how we understand places and the people who move through them? Would you like to help build a new generation of geographic models grounded in how people actually perceive and remember cities? Do you enjoy working at the boundary between machine learning and real-world application?

ReCoGNiSe (Representations of Cognitive Geography for Navigating Sustainable Neighbourhoods) is a five-year, €2m research programme funded by a European Research Council Consolidator Grant. ReCoGNiSe starts from a critical disconnect at the heart of geographic analysis: that the digital representations of space on which spatial data are built do not reflect how places are perceived and remembered. The project aims to initiate a step-change in how geographic space is represented, building new representations of spatial features and relations, grounded in spatial cognition and computational neuroscience.

We are looking to recruit a passionate researcher to lead our work on cognitive feature representations using foundation models. You will use a vast array of data to build rich, multimodal representations of urban cognitive features, capturing facets such as visual salience, cultural significance, function, and locational importance. This will involve working with general-purpose language, vision-language and multimodal models, alongside geospatial foundation models. Your representations will provide the foundation for the project's cognitive map representations. Working with the wider project team, you will adapt approaches to reflect newly collected data on how features are perceived differently across populations and over time, and integrate with other work on constructing models of spatial learning. They will also underpin the project's open-source releases.

Candidates will require expertise in deep learning and foundation models, ideally applied to geospatial or human-generated data. Given this work sits at the interface of GeoAI, geography and neuroscience, we are particularly seeking applicants who enjoy working across disciplinary boundaries, are committed to open and responsible AI, and are keen to engage with theory from geography and spatial cognition.

This role will be hosted within the Mobility Science Lab, in the Institute for Spatial Data Science (ISDS) at the School of Geography. As well as working closely with Prof Ed Manley and the wider ReCoGNiSe research team (totalling three Research Fellows and two PhD students), you will collaborate with Dr Weiming Huang (University of Leeds), who brings expertise in foundation models and GeoAI, and Prof Hugo Spiers (UCL), who brings expertise in the neuroscience of spatial cognition. You will also benefit from the project's international network of collaborators in spatial cognition, GeoAI and urban science.

To discuss the post further or for any queries you may have, please contact:

Ed Manley, Professor of Urban Analytics - Email: E.J.Manley@Leeds.ac.uk

Senior Research Associate in Scene and Video Understanding
 Apply
The role

A strong and vibrant research team with steady-stream publications in high-calibre venues is looking for a postdoctoral researcher to develop novel approaches to 3D/4D scene and video understanding in conversational settings. The position is funded by the EU project WeHear, a collaboration led by Denmark Technical University (DTU). The overall project focuses on audio-visual understanding for smart hearing aid. This role though is for expertise in core computer vision, focusing on scene modelling, understanding, human tracking and forecasting (of humans and objects) from egocentric vision.

You will be working closely with Dima and Wei-Hong on their active research. Check their research interests and projects at: http://dimadamen.github.io/ and https://weihongli-ac.github.io.

Prior expertise in video understanding, computer vision and deep learning methods with a strong publication track record is expected, including first-author publications in CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/ICASSP/PAMI/IJCV/NeurIPS/ICLR.

What will you be doing?

Conducting novel research in 3D/4D scene and video understanding – contributing novel research on designing, training and evaluating video understanding models. This will include hands-on research using the latest deep learning approaches.
Preparing API packages with low latency that will be integrated with partner demonstrations on quarterly basis. 
Presenting your work in regular meetings, taking feedback and integrating the goals of the proect into your individual research directions.
Publishing in top-tier venues (conferences and journals). Communicating your work to the best possible audience.
Collaborating with other researchers (postdocs and faculty) in the WeHear project.
Co-advising junior PGR students

You should apply if

PhD [near submission, submitted or graduated] in 3D/4D Scene, Video Understanding, preferably with expertise in 3D/4D scene understanding or video understanding or equivalent research experience in an academic, industrial or clinical setting equivalent to a PhD.
Prior degree in computer science, engineering or mathematics
Detailed knowledge of video understanding state-of-the-art, approaches, datasets and problems, preferably with expertise in egocentric datasets.
Prior knowledge of egocentric audio-visual devices that work in real time like Meta Aria Glasses (Gen1 or Gen2).
Experience in handling video and/or 3D scene data, for learning and inference
Experience in modelling deep learning approaches
Experience and evidence of publishing at high-calibre conferences and journals (at least one first-author paper in a major venue – CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/ICASSP/NeurIPs/PAMI/IJCV/Neurips/ICLR in the past 3 years).
Excellent programming skills (Python)
Proficiency in deep learning frameworks (PyTorch)

Research Associate in Digital Optical Tomography - Diagnostic Objective Measures for Hearing Device Users - 'Little Listeners' Project (Fixed Term - 9 months)

Applications are invited for:

A post-doctoral Research Associate in Optical Brain Measurements, and Auditory Neuroscience to be part of the SOUND (Sensory Optimisation Using Neuroscience for Devices) laboratory in Clinical Neurosciences at the University of Cambridge to work on our 'Little Listeners' project which uses High Density - Digital Optical Tomography (HD-DOT) to measure brain activity in response to audio-visual speech stimuli (using different degrees of auditory or visual degradation in different conditions). The goal of the work is to map out the developmental patterns in a longitudinal study and to compare results to early markers of speech and language and cognitive development. In the first place this research is funded by the Biomedical Research Centre but there is a possibility of the contract being extended following the receipt of further ongoing funding.

The ideal candidate will have a background of working in objective and behavioural measures with young children and have a good understanding of hearing loss, hearing devices and acoustic analyses of sound. It is very important that the candidate can calibrate auditory stimuli, can work with children and their families and develop a close working rapport with clinicians. It would be ideal if the candidate has the skills to be able to learn how to analyse recordings to determine patterns of brain response.

The post holder will be based in the Clinical Neuroscience Department (SOUND Lab - https://www-neurosciences.medschl.cam.ac.uk/sound-lab/) on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus, Addenbrookes hospital site working closely with Professor Debi Vickers and other members of the Little Listeners team. The position will be affiliated with the Addenbrookes Cochlear Implant Programme and the Cambridge Hearing Group.

For questions relating to the post, please contact Professor Debi Vickers - dav1000@cam.ac.uk.

Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 9 months (0.6 FTE) in the first instance.

The Managers of the Herchel Smith Fund invite applications for up to two Postdoctoral Research Fellowships in Biophysics & Geophysics, hosted by the Departments of University of Cambridge.

Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 3 years in the first instance.

The Fellows will be able to undertake their research in the following departments:

Physics (https://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/)

Department of Earth Sciences (https://www.esc.cam.ac.uk/)

DAMTP ' Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics (https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/)

The Fellowships commence on 1 October 2027 (or by negotiation), are tenable for up to three years and support full-time independent research in Cambridge, usually in collaboration with established research groups.

Funding: The Fellowship stipend will be on the University's Postdoctoral Research Associate scale, grade 7, scale point 41 per annum, with an annual research allowance of up to £15,000.

Eligibility: In accordance with Dr Smith's will, candidature is limited to candidates who have obtained their PhD degree, or equivalent, within the last three years at any university excluding Cambridge and Harvard.

Departmental requirements

Applicants must consult their proposed Department well before the closing date, identify a suitable academic host and secure the agreement of their proposed Principal Investigator (PI) before applying. They must also ensure their research proposal aligns with the host research group.

To obtain the mandatory departmental support letter, applicants must contact the relevant Department at least two weeks before submission (or earlier if departmental deadlines apply), providing their proposed application and a supporting statement from their agreed academic host.

Applicants must check departmental requirements and internal deadlines directly:

Physics: fellowships@phy.cam.ac.uk

Earth Sciences: grants@esc.cam.ac.uk

DAMTP: grants@damtp.cam.ac.uk

Earth Sciences and DAMTP applicants must also email a copy of their completed application to their Department. This does not replace submission through the University's recruitment system.

Required application documents

All applications must be submitted online through the University's recruitment system and include:

Host Support Letter: Each candidate is required to submit a letter from an SPS Department confirming its willingness to host and support the candidate's research during the Fellowship. Candidates should contact the relevant Department before submitting their application, providing a copy of their proposed application and a statement from the member of academic staff who has agreed to host the candidate and their project. The Host Support Letter will then be supplied by the Head of Department. Applicants must obtain this letter in time to include it in their online application.

Research project summary: One page summary of your proposed project, including the name of the SPS Department which you hope to join.

Research project description: A detailed description (maximum of 4 pages) of the proposed project. Applicants should consult the relevant member of academic staff and/or other resources to ensure that the proposal is appropriately related to the group they hope to join.

Curriculum vitae: Maximum of three pages outlining academic career, qualifications and full list of publications to date; please include hyperlinks of 3 best publications (not full copies).

References (two required): Letters from two referees, neither of whom may be the proposed host PI. Confidential references may be emailed directly to herchelsmith@admin.cam.ac.uk by the closing date.

Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Closing date: 17 January 2027

Selection outcome: Successful candidates will be contacted by March 2027.

Enquiries: herchelsmith@admin.cam.ac.uk

Further information: https://www.physsci.cam.ac.uk/research

Please quote reference AK51749 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

About us:

The School of Academic Psychiatry brings together five leading clinical departments: Addictions, Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, Forensic and Neurodevelopmental Science, Psychological Medicine, and Psychosis Studies. Our community includes more than 100 Principal Investigators and a vibrant research portfolio supported by £30–40 million in active grants. Across the School, our work spans the full breadth of psychiatry—from public policy to molecular genetics, from perinatal mental health to old age, and from psychological therapies to advanced brain imaging.

This role sits within the Department of Psychological Medicine, at the Centre for Healthy Brain Ageing (CHBA).

At CHBA, we are united by a simple but powerful goal: to help people maintain good mental and cognitive health as they age, and to ensure that older adults—including our own parents and grandparents—receive the highest standard of care should they develop psychological or psychiatric conditions. We are a friendly, motivated, and collaborative team, committed to nurturing the next generation of researchers in our field.

We aim to advance the development of biomarkers for neurocognitive disorders and to create innovative approaches for the early diagnosis of cognitive decline, Alzheimer’s disease, and ageing-related psychiatric conditions. As a centre of excellence for clinical trials, we support the development of novel therapeutic strategies and technologies while improving patient access to both established and emerging treatments.

About the role:

The post holder will play a key role in supporting the Centre for Healthy Brain Ageing ongoing portfolio of clinical and translational research studies. Responsibilities will include overseeing day-to-day study operations, ensuring adherence to protocols and regulatory standards, and facilitating communication between investigators, research assistants, and collaborators across sites. The successful candidate will conduct cognitive and clinical assessments, contribute to data collection, management, and analysis, and support the preparation of research outputs including reports and publications. They will maintain regular contact with study participants and their relatives, ensuring a high standard of participant engagement and retention. In addition, the post holder will assist in the development and maintenance of essential study documentation and processes to ensure compliance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and institutional policies. They will also provide administrative and research support for the management of multiple studies, working under the supervision of Prof Dag Aarsland and contributing to the scientific and operational success of the Centre’s research portfolio.

This is a full time (40 hours per week), and you will be offered a 12mth FTC.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the  Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you:

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

MBChB/ MBBS or equivalent
Full GMC registration with valid license to practice
Strong interpersonal, oral and written communication skills with the ability to convey goals of research to lay people and communicate complex information in clear and easily understandable way to a lay audience, including those with cognitive impairment
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team, with strong problem-solving skills and ability to take initiative
Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and excellent attention to detail and accuracy, with strong administrative and record-keeping skills
Experience running a Clinical Trial of an Investigative Medicinal Product (CTIMP) or acceptability studies of novel interventions
Experience of reviewing ECG reports independently
Experience of conducting Lumbar puncture procedure

Desirable criteria

Ability to collect and process biological samples
Experience of Intrathecal Administration
Experience of preparing academic papers for publication and ability to conduct and present scientific research in the form of posters and oral presentations
Prior involvement in multi-institutional or international research collaborations
Clinical Experience and experience of working with people with dementia, and sensitive to the needs of people with dementia and their carers

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. At times, this will include balancing rights and beliefs that can feel in tension.

Post Doctoral Research Associate

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us

King's College London is one of the world's leading research-intensive universities. Within the  Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine, the School of Basic & Biomedical Sciences (BMBS) hosts the  Randall Centre for Cell & Molecular Biophysics, an internationally leading centre for cell biology, biophysics and structural biology.

About the role

Applications are invited for an experienced postdoctoral scientist to join a distinctive fellowship between King's College London (King's) and UCB. The Fellow will combine an academically anchored research programme in Professor Peter Zammit's group running in parallel with an embedded role supporting UCB's Translational Medicine activities in neuromuscular disease. This structure is designed to provide experience across academic discovery and biopharmaceutical translation while maintaining clear, complementary workstreams at each institution.

The Zammit group will focus on facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), the third most common inherited myopathy. We have identified several pathways that are deregulated in FSHD (e.g. Mitochondrial Respiratory Chain Function is crucial for Muscle Toxicity in Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy: doi:  https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.25.690559). This aspect of the work will further investigate the role of such pathways in pathology, with an emphasis on those controlling cellular bioenergetics and metabolism.

During the simultaneous UCB secondment, the Fellow will contribute neuromuscular disease expertise and translational insight across research and early development. Working with cross-functional colleagues, the Fellow will help evaluate disease biology, human evidence, multi-omics data, biomarkers, patient populations, clinical feasibility, emerging therapeutic approaches and the translational rationale for novel targets and preclinical candidates. The role will connect mechanistic evidence with testable clinical hypotheses and support clear, evidence-based recommendations for project teams and decision-making forums.

The successful candidate will bring strong experimental expertise in muscle cell and molecular biology and the ability to integrate diverse scientific evidence. They will communicate with clarity, work effectively across academic and industry environments, and handle confidential information in accordance with the applicable institutional requirements.

This fellowship offers a unique opportunity to develop a career at the interface of academic research and biopharmaceutical translation. The post holder will have access to training, seminars, libraries, research facilities and professional networks across both King’s College London and UCB, supporting their development in skeletal muscle biology, neuromuscular disease research and therapeutic translation.

This is a full-time post employed by King’s College London, with the post holder seconded part-time to UCB. For Postdoctoral Fellows, 60% of working time will be allocated to the UCB project and 40% to King’s College London duties. The working arrangement and schedule will be agreed jointly by King’s College London and UCB. This postholder will be on a fixed-term contract until from 2nd January 2027 until 1st January 2031.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the  Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

An awarded PhD, research doctorate or equivalent in muscle biology, molecular/cellular biology, biomedical sciences or a closely related discipline. Medically qualified applicants should also demonstrate equivalent research training and experience.
Substantial hands-on research experience in cell and molecular biology, including mammalian cell culture and protein-analysis methods. Demonstrated experience in mitochondrial biology, cellular metabolism, bioenergetics or closely related functional assays.
Strong understanding of neuromuscular disease biology, with the ability to connect molecular mechanisms to human disease and therapeutic hypotheses.
Ability to design rigorous experiments, interpret complex results, troubleshoot methods and maintain complete, reproducible research records. Commitment to research integrity, inclusive working practices, confidentiality and responsible handling of data and intellectual property.
Ability to critically evaluate and integrate evidence from experimental studies, human biology, omics datasets and the scientific literature.
Evidence of scientific productivity, including authorship of peer-reviewed research outputs and effective presentation of scientific findings.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex concepts to multidisciplinary academic and industry audiences.
Effective planning, prioritisation and delivery across parallel workstreams, with a collaborative, proactive and solution-oriented approach.

Desirable criteria

Direct research experience in FSHD or another muscular dystrophy.
Experience analysing transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic or other high-dimensional datasets using R, Python or established bioinformatics workflows.
Experience with patient-derived cells, primary human muscle models, disease-relevant phenotyping or translational biomarker research.
Understanding of translational medicine, target validation, drug discovery or early clinical development in an industry or collaborative setting.
Experience coordinating collaborations, supervising junior researchers or contributing to grant applications.

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.

The University of Nottingham seeks applications for a Research Associate/ Fellow in Metallic and Ceramic Powder manufacturing guided by thermodynamic modelling or density functional theory simulation. The researcher will be joining the Centre of Excellence in Coatings and Surface Engineering with 20 full-time researchers. The Centre hosts an EPSRC doctoral training centre, EPSRC Network plus and two European Marie Curie Doctoral Training Networks along with 25 active industry-funded projects. 

The successful candidate will perform research aimed at using spray drying, agglomeration and sintering and wet chemistry methods to manufacture ceramic and metallic powder for thermal spray. The candidate will develop new powder compositions guided by thermocalc modelling, characterise the powder using advanced electron microscopy and x-ray diffraction, and carry out appropriate mechanical and environmental tests on the manufacturing coatings. 

Experience in spray drying and thermodynamic modelling is essential for this position. You must have (or about to complete) a PhD in Materials Engineering or an equivalent degree. You will have good interpersonal skills and the ability to work in a team to tight deadlines. The CV and/or cover letter should clearly exemplify how you meet the criteria highlighted herein and in the Role Profile and describe your motivation for applying for this position.

The proposed research is leading-edge, and expected to lead to high-quality publications and industrial applications, making this an ideal training opportunity for an academic or industry career. 

The post is for a period of 12 months, subject to renewal. The position is available from 1st Dec 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter. The post is part of an EPSRC project, AdCerap, the ATI-funded project, Thermos, and a Rolls-Royce direct industry-funded project on new coatings. 

Please direct informal enquiries to Professor Tanvir Hussain (Professor of Coatings and Surface Engineering) at Tanvir.Hussain@nottingham.ac.uk.
 
 Please note that applications sent directly to these email addresses will not be accepted.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

We are seeking an independent and highly motivated Research Associate to join an MRC-funded project at the interface of developmental biology, stem cell biology and disease modelling. The successful candidate will use human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) differentiation approaches to investigate the developmental dynamics of human enteric nervous system (ENS) progenitors and their contribution to Hirschsprung disease. This project is a close collaboration with the group of Conor McCann at the UCL Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health in London.

 

Applicants must hold a PhD (or be close to completion / have equivalent postdoctoral work experience) in an area related to stem cell/developmental biology. Demonstrable experience in hPSC culture, immunocytochemistry/imaging and quantitative PCR (qPCR) is essential. Experience in neural or neural crest differentiation would be an advantage. The successful candidate will be highly motivated, organised and capable of working independently as well as collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research team. Excellent interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills, together with a commitment to high-quality research, are also essential.

Main duties and responsibilities

Determine novel research objectives as experiments progress and initiate and implement relevant programme of research.

Disseminate research findings/results through the production of papers for high-quality journals and presentation either in-house or at national/international conferences or seminars.

Efficiently manage time, materials, finance and equipment.

Provide support to PI for research proposals and funding applications.

Supervise or co-supervise undergraduate/postgraduate project students and/or PhD students.

Delegate and monitor the work of research students.

Deal with reactive requests relating to supervision of research staff and students.

Participate in consortium meetings and seminars, in particular with collaborators

Plan up to several months in advance to meet deadlines for journal publications and to prepare presentations and papers for collaboration meetings and conferences.

As a member of staff you will be encouraged to make ethical decisions in your role, embedding the University sustainability strategy into your working activities wherever
